business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Reverse Logistics and Returned Goods Quality Grading

Agreement between the Kingdom of Spain and the United Mexican States on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 1995, in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April 2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (BOE No. 92, 29 April 2010); Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May 2014, approving the Regulation implementing Law 10/2010 (BOE No. 111, 7 May 2014), as amended by Royal Decree 609/2023; Articles 28 and 29 of Law 10/2010 impose the identification, verification, retention and declaration of beneficial ownership; Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD) is transposed in relevant parts; the Spanish Central Commercial Register and the incorporating notary maintain UBO records, with SEPBLAC acting as the operational AML/CFT supervisor.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the corporate charter / articles of association of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent administrative authority in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the foreign jurisdiction is not a Hague Convention state, full Consular Legalization via the Spanish diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence / good standing of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent administrative authority in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if not a Hague state, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney from the foreign corporate shareholder to the Spanish incorporator or notary-appointed representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's registered legal representative before a notarial authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if not a Hague state, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each director, proxy holder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, passport office or police authority of the holder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy notarized in Spain; original identity document presented at notary appointment; apostille not required for identity documents but notarization is mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Evidence of lawful source of funds / bank account certificate for the minimum capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Spanish bank or EU/EEA credit institution, or documented alternative payment account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-certified document; apostille not required, but the notary must receive the original or certified banking statement before incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each director, shareholder above 10%, UBO and authorized signatory against the unified Spanish PEP data directory maintained by SEPBLAC, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists under Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and Council Regulation (EU) 2580/2001, and the OFAC SDN list as an international market-benchmark standard; the KYC file must record screening date, source database and any adverse media result; enhanced due diligence is compulsory if any positive hit occurs, if the UBO is PEP, or if the shareholder resides in a non-OECD jurisdiction; the notary must confirm the identification has been completed before executing the incorporation deed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - Certificación de Denominaciones Sociales (online platform administered by the Spanish Registrars' Association, accessible through notaries and accredited legal representatives)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in Spanish; a foreign-language name is permitted only if expressed in Latin script using the Spanish alphabet and diacritic conventions; non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into the official Spanish registered form; the corporate name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing Spanish company; the legal form suffix 'S.L.' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' is required in all contractual and registry documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms contrary to public order, criminal law or misleading commercial use
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may immediately request an alternative name certificate through the same online RMC portal; a second rejection may be challenged by submitting a written administrative appeal ('recurso gubernativo') to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (formerly DGRN) at the Spanish Ministry of Justice within one month of notification, attaching the negative certificate and evidence of compliance; after exhaustion of the administrative route, an appeal may be filed before the Audiencia Nacional under Ley 39/2015; the notary must be notified of the final certificate before drafting the deed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is legally permissible in Spain for a low-risk reverse logistics/returned goods grading SL if the address is a real Spanish postal address capable of receiving official notifications, the central administration and corporate records are kept at a verifiable location, and at least one appointed representative in Spain has physical access to that address; the tax administration will not accept a virtual office as a substitute for actual management presence where this would incorrectly create a domestic substance shield.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated low-to-moderate risk: approximately 5-10% for a clean, simple low-risk SL; 15-25% if the company invoices related parties, has no separate physical administrative records, or is flagged in a pre-incorporation risk review; unannounced inspections may be carried out by Agencia Tributaria, SEPBLAC, or municipal police authorities under applicable law.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name certificate application and issuance fee (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff payable at the time of online filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of incorporation deed, bylaws, UBO declaration and corporate resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard SL incorporation with cross-border shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fee for execution of the public incorporation deed (escritura de constitución)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff set by the Spanish National Notary Association, variable with capital and document pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry registration fee (inscripción de la sociedad in the Registro Mercantil)
Bank account opening and capital deposit certificate for the legal minimum capital contribution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish bank acting under Banco de España regulation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial bank charge; may be zero for fully digital onboarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate parent documents, official sworn translation and courier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the country of origin; sworn translator in Spain; courier service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for four apostilled documents with Spanish translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation PEP, OFAC, UN sanctions screening and due diligence report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for one corporate entity with two UBO declarations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax opening and census declaration to Agencia Tributaria (CIF/IVA alta)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory no-fee filing; lawyer handling fee covered under the legal drafting line item

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered office service (domiciliación social) for a virtual office address in Spain
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a one-year virtual office contract, excluding warehouse operating costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, 'LSC'), Articles 19-22 (incorporation), Article 4 (minimum capital), Articles 28, 58-59 (registered office), and Articles 102-104, 209-233 (administration and appointment of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name clearance) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (statutory inscription)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) granted before a Spanish Notary and subsequently inscribed in the Registro Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL minimum capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind at incorporation; capital must be deposited in escrow at a Spanish credit entity or held by the notary pending execution of the deed, and the deposit certificate must be attached to the deed. Alternatively, under Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece'), incorporation as Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva (SLFS) is permitted with EUR 1 minimum capital, subject to a mandatory legal reserve of 20% of annual profits until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], S.L. — Unanimously resolved by the founding members: 1. Share subscription: All member quotas comprising the EUR 3,000 statutory share capital are fully subscribed and paid in; quota allocation is ratified. 2. Registered office: The legal seat and administrative center is fixed at [Address], Spain, for all corporate, tax, and regulatory purposes. 3. Officers: [Full Name] is appointed Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) for an indefinite term with the full powers of Article 233 of the Spanish Capital Companies Act. 4. Delegation: The Administrator is authorized to open bank accounts, execute registry filings, apply for tax and labor identifiers, and take all steps to commence operations. All resolutions unanimously approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — online via the notaries' and registrars' electronic platform (www.registradores.org) or CIRCE portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a telematic application for a Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social requesting up to three alternative corporate names; specify ISIC 5229 reverse logistics as the object; pay the administrative fee; the certificate is ordinarily issued within one to three business days and is valid for three months, during which the deed must be executed.
required_dossiers: National identity document (DNI/NIE) or passport of each founding member
Completed official application form (solicitud de certificación de denominación)
Up to three proposed company names in order of preference
Proof of payment of the RMC fee
Brief description of the corporate purpose (ISIC 5229 reverse logistics and returned-goods grading)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the denomination is refused on grounds of identity or confusing similarity with an existing registered name, resubmit the application the same day with substitute denominations. If the certificate expires before deed execution, obtain a fresh certificate before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit of the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit entity (bank) or the Notary acting as escrow depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account under the name '[Company Name], S.L. en formación' and deposit the full statutory capital (minimum EUR 3,000, or the subscribed amount for an SLFS). Obtain a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) stating the holder, amount, and date. Alternatively, hand the capital to the notary before execution of the deed; the notarial certificate of deposit will be incorporated into the notarial protocol.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all subscribing members
Provisional corporate name certificate issued by RMC
Draft articles of association (estatutos sociales)
Bank deposit certificate or notarial deposit acknowledgment
Source-of-funds declaration for AML purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is defective or refused, instruct the credit entity to reissue a corrected certificate or transfer the funds to another authorized bank and obtain a fresh certificate before the notary appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) chosen by the founding members
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the valid name certificate, deposit certificate, articles of association, and the shareholders' identification. The notary verifies legal capacity, reads the deed, records unanimous consent, and executes the Escritura Pública de Constitución. Request several certified copies (testimonios): one for the Registro Mercantil, one for the tax office, one for the bank, and one for company records. The notary will also file the deed with the commercial registry electronically where available.
required_dossiers: Valid name clearance certificate from RMC
Bank or notarial certificate of capital deposit
Executed draft of the articles of association (estatutos)
DNI/NIE or passport of all shareholders and of the appointed administrator
Proof of payment of notary fees (arancel notarial)
Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) statement and AML declaration for the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises an objection (e.g., defective clause, missing signature, or inconsistency in the statutes), cure the defect by executing a rectification addendum before the same notary and obtain re-issued certified copies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Corporate Transaction Tax (ITPAJD — Operaciones Societarias)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria de la Comunidad Autónoma (regional tax office — Dirección General de Tributos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of the deed execution, self-assess and pay the 1% capital duty under Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados (Modelo 600, Operaciones Societarias) applicable to capital increases and incorporation. Submit the certified copy of the deed and the name certificate; obtain the stamped/validated copy (ejemplar sellado) required for the commercial registry filing.
required_dossiers: Modelo 600 self-assessment form
Certified copy (testimonio) of the notarial deed
Company name certificate
Provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) of the company in formation
Proof of capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regional tax office detects underpayment or requests additional documentation, file a complementary return (declaración complementaria) within the voluntary period to avoid surcharges and expedite the stamped copy required for registry inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first certified copy of the deed, together with the stamped Modelo 600, the official application form (instancia), and identification of the appointees. Pay the registry fee (arancel del Registro Mercantil). The registrar examines the deed for legal compliance and issues the inscription (inscripción), after which the company acquires full legal personality and is bound as from that date; obtain a certificación literal or nota simple as proof of registration.
required_dossiers: First certified copy (testimonio) of the public deed
Stamped Modelo 600 evidencing payment of ITPAJD
Application form addressed to the Registrar
Provisional NIF of the company
DNI/NIE of the appointed administrator
Proof of payment of registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a negative calificación (defects note), cure each defect either by submitting a rectification deed or by supplying the missing documents within the granted period; if the qualification is deemed unlawful, appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF and Employer (Social Security) Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the commercial registry inscription is obtained, file Modelo 036 (change of census data) with AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF, attaching the registry certificate and the deed. With the definitive NIF, register the company as an employer by applying online through the Sistema RED for a Código de Cuenta de Cotización (CCC) using forms TA.7 and TA.9. Open the operational corporate bank account and configure payment rails (Local ACH / Airwallex) once the NIF is final.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 (census registration/update) signed by the legal representative
Certificado de inscripción issued by the Registro Mercantil
Certified copy of the deed and powers of attorney
DNI/NIE of the legal representative
TGSS forms TA.7 / TA.9 and CCC application
Lease contract or title document for the registered office and warehouse premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT requires verification of the physical premises, present the lease contract and facilitate a site inspection; if the definitive NIF is not yet issued, continue routine banking with the provisional NIF but complete the definitive registration before any customs or cross-border trade activity, since imports/exports require the final NIF.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality where the logistics/grading facility is located (Área de Licencias, Urbanismo y Actividades), with prior or parallel notification to the Dirección General de Industria of the corresponding Comunidad Autónoma for registration of the industrial establishment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura y Actividad (Municipal Economic Activity and Opening License) governed by Ley 7/1985, de 2 de abril, Reguladora de las Bases del Régimen Local (LBRL), the autonomous community's activity-licensing legislation, and the applicable municipal ordenanza de actividades (for facilities above a local threshold, a Declaración Responsable or Comunicación Previa may be accepted in lieu of a prior license, subject to municipal verification)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) and the competent environmental authority of the Autonomous Community (e.g., Consejería de Medio Ambiente), under Ley 21/2013, de 9 de diciembre, de evaluación ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier 3 — Low-impact environmental registration (comunicación ambiental previa or régimen de comunicación) for reverse-logistics and returned-goods grading facilities with warehousing below 1,000 m² rooftop and no hazardous-waste treatment; a simplified environmental impact assessment (EIA simplificada, Ley 21/2013 Annex II) is triggered only if operations include waste treatment exceeding 500 t/annum, involve hazardous returned goods, or are sited within Natura 2000 or other protected zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Ley 7/2022, de 8 de abril, de residuos y suelos contaminados: returned e-waste (RAEE/WEEE) must flow exclusively through authorized producer compliance schemes with full chain-of-custody records; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from grading, cleaning, and sealing operations must remain below 2 t/annum (RD 117/2003) unless a VOC authorization is obtained; wastewater discharged into the municipal sewer must comply with the municipal discharge ordinance and the applicable hydrological plan parameters (TSS ≤ 500 mg/L, COD ≤ 700 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, pH 6-9); no untreated hazardous effluent may be released; packaging waste recovery quotas under Ley 7/2022 (minimum 65% recycling by 2025 target) apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety engineering certificate (certificado técnico de protección contra incendios) under RD 513/2017, verified by an Organismo de Control Autorizado (OCA) for storage warehouses exceeding 250 m²; structural load certificate for racking systems and floor-load-bearing capacity issued by a competent architect/engineer; occupational risk-prevention evaluation (evaluación de riesgos laborales) under Ley 31/1995 and workplace health-and-safety clearance before deployment of employees; municipal civil-protection (protección civil) inspection if the site qualifies as a major-accident or large-storage installation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity obtaining a Spanish branch, permanent establishment, or VAT nexus must obtain a Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for non-resident legal entities. Application forms are submitted to AEAT, including Form 036/037, notarial and registry documents evidencing the SL's incorporation and legal existence, power of attorney for the tax representative, and for VAT purposes, Form 036 registration as a taxable person. An SL incorporated in Spain receives a provisional CIF/NIF at the notary stage and a definitive NIF after filing Form 030 with the Commercial Registry and AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not have a US-style check-the-box regime. An SL is automatically a resident taxpayer subject to Corporation Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at a standard 25% rate on worldwide income. Available elections include the Option for Tax Consolidation for group companies with at least 75% direct/indirect ownership, the special reduced Corporation Tax rate of 15% for newly created qualifying S.L.s under Arts. 29 and 29 bis of LIS, and the VAT Group Registration election provided by Art. 163 quarterdecies LIVA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA / VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 - no general VAT registration exemption threshold exists in Spain. Any taxable person, including a non-resident reverse-logistics operator, habitually supplying goods or services in Spanish territory (excluding Ceuta, Melilla, and the Canary Islands for IVA purposes) must register for Spanish VAT before commencing taxable activity. The EU One Stop Shop regime reduces the need for separate registration for intra-EU distance sales and imports not exceeding EUR 150, but Spanish domestic reverse-logistics services with a fixed establishment or PE require full Spanish VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates structured electronic invoicing for B2B transactions between entrepreneurs/professionals under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), effective through implementing regulations on interoperability. Large taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04 and VAT groups are subject to the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) system, whereby VAT invoice records must be transmitted to AEAT via certified XML/Facturae web-services APIs within 4 business days (8 days for invoices). Royal Decree 1007/2023 (Verifactu) requires compliant billing software capable of generating QR-coded/authenticated invoice records and making them available to AEAT on request. Spain does not operate a centralized pre-clearance stamping regime for every invoice, but SII/Verifactu compliance is mandatory and subject to periodic electronic monitoring.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A reverse-logistics and returned-goods operator may apply 0% VAT (exempt with credit/deductibility) on goods physically exported from the EU to a third-country destination, including export-related services such as transport, loading, warehousing, quality grading, and handling performed for the exporter and directly linked to the export movement. Services supplied to a non-EU business customer for the fulfillment of export stores/return hubs and reverse logistics services may also be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under B2B reverse-charge rules where the recipient is a taxable person in a third country, provided the service is not physically used in Spain. All zero-rating claims require delivery of goods outside the EU within the statutory period and receipt of documentary evidence of export within 90 days from supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Single Administrative Document (DUA) stamped by Spanish Customs
Bill of Lading, CMR road consignment note, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from EU customs territory
Proof of arrival / customs clearance in the destination country (if available)
Warehouse outgoing / return-shipment approval records tying the exported goods to the reverse-logistics order
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/PSP transfer confirmation demonstrating receipt of export consideration in a bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT rigorously audits export zero-rating claims. Failure to substantiate exportation with the required DUA and shipping documents triggers retrospective VAT assessment at 21% on the full invoiced amount plus late-payment interest. Fraud, false documents, or sham circular export/return schemes constitute tax evasion under Art. 305 of the Criminal Code, subject to penalties of 2-6 years imprisonment, fines of up to 6 times the defrauded amount, and loss of tax benefits. Administrative penalties range from 50% to 150% of the VAT loss depending on persistence and concealment; the taxpayer also loses deduction rights and may be barred from obtaining VAT refunds pending full remediation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) supervises Spanish credit institutions, payment systems and balance-of-payments statistical reporting; the Foreign Investment Registry is administered by the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones within the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise; the European Central Bank (ECB) holds ultimate euro-area monetary policy and exchange-rate policy competence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies because Spain is a euro-area member with unrestricted capital and current-account mobility under Article 63 TFEU. The euro is freely convertible; dividend and profit remittance from a Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders requires no prior authorisation, no conversion quota and no profit-repatriation permit. Residual obligations are administrative and statistical only: residents must report cross-border transactions to Banco de España through their bank, with individual declaration required for transactions of EUR 50,000 or above; foreign direct investment into Spain above EUR 250,000 must be declared ex post on Form DGI-01 to the Foreign Investment Registry within 30 days; investments originating from tax-haven listed jurisdictions above EUR 50,000 require immediate post-closing verification. Convertibility hurdles for profit remittance are effectively nil as long as corporate registries and the 25% corporate income tax position are current.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain maintains a zero-surrender, zero-mandatory-conversion regime. There is no statutory repatriation deadline, no fixed conversion ratio and no obligation to liquidate export receipts into EUR; an SL may collect and hold foreign-currency proceeds indefinitely in accounts with resident credit institutions or EU/EEA e-money institutions. The only binding requirements are evidential retention (export contracts, customs declarations, return-authorisation records) and Banco de España statistical reporting for receipts and conversions at or above EUR 50,000.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Certificado de Desembolso for initial share capital) / Operational multi-currency Account
Operational Account (EUR and USD) with integrated treasury and LatAm correspondent network
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with FX forwards and hedging facilities
Operational SEPA Account supporting virtual-IBAN settlement and payout automation
Digital Operational Account with remote onboarding capability for EEA-resident directors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as a complementary settlement layer, but not as a substitute for a licensed Spanish credit institution. Airwallex and comparable EU-regulated e-money institutions passport into Spain under PSD2 and may operate multi-currency payment accounts, execute FX conversion and access local clearing rails (SEPA, US ACH/Fedwire, UK FPS/CHAPS, Mexico SPEI, Brazil PIX). Hard constraints: an EMI cannot extend credit or pay interest, client funds are not deposit-guaranteed and are not covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD), Spanish resident companies must report foreign accounts on Modelo 720 when year-end balances exceed EUR 50,000 per account class, and Tier-1 Spanish banks commonly impose enhanced source-of-funds review on flows sourced from EMI virtual IBANs. Recommended posture: maintain the primary operating account at Santander, BBVA or CaixaBank, and use Airwallex exclusively for low-value cross-border payouts and Latin-American receipt collection, with same-day ERP reconciliation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is technically possible for EU/EEA-resident directors using eIDAS-qualified electronic identification and video KYC, but the prevailing Tier-1 Spanish bank practice requires an in-person KYC interview of at least one director or the single authorised signatory at the branch, or notarial identity authentication in Spain supported by an apostilled power of attorney for remote directors. Non-EEA directors are almost always subject to a mandatory physical appearance rule or an equivalent attestation from a correspondent bank. The practical blueprint is a two-day onboarding visit to Madrid or Barcelona to open accounts at Banco Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank and Sabadell, carrying the notarial deed, Registro Mercantil certificate, NIE cards, UBO declaration, capital-deposit certificate and a board resolution defining signatory authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SL with low paid-in capital versus projected high-volume cross-border reverse-logistics flows; possible red flag for trade-based money laundering or inflated sales declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) notarial deed of incorporation and Registro Mercantil registration certificate; (2) bank certificate of share-capital deposit; (3) business plan evidencing unit economics of returns processing, quality grading and resale; (4) signed warehouse lease and logistics SOPs; (5) executed client contracts with e-commerce platforms or freight forwarders; (6) 24-month cash-flow forecast reviewed by an external accountant; (7) proof of commercial liability and cargo insurance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity arising from non-resident shareholders organised through multiple intermediate holding layers, nominee structures, or domiciliation in tax-haven jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) formal UBO declaration in the statutory Spanish template (declaración de titular real) under Ley 10/2010; (2) registry extract of the Spanish company and available shareholder registries; (3) ownership chart with exact percentage stakes down to ultimate natural persons; (4) passport, NIE and tax-residence certificates of all ultimate beneficial owners; (5) independent sanctions and PEP screening report issued within the last 30 days; (6) signed undertaking that no shares are held through bearer instruments or undisclosed trusts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictional exposure: counterparties or payment originators in Latin-American or Caribbean jurisdictions with limited AML enforcement or classification as tax havens under Royal Decree 1080/1991.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) enhanced due-diligence (EDD) questionnaires for each high-risk client, supplier and payment intermediary; (2) jurisdiction-specific risk matrix with mitigating controls; (3) underlying trade evidence including invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading and tracking data demonstrating genuine reverse-logistics transactions; (4) quarterly transaction-monitoring and AML audit reports; (5) confirmation that no payments originate in EU/CFT blacklisted jurisdictions without a licensed intermediary; (6) external legal opinion on the FATF compliance status of material counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Circular refund payment patterns inherent to returned-merchandise processing, where inflows from platform refunds and outflows to graders or repairers may be mischaracterised as layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) contract chain proving ownership and liability for returned goods; (2) operating procedure manual for returns authentication, RMA-log creation and quality grading with one-to-one parcel references; (3) completed sample transaction file showing the full return lifecycle from customer complaint to refund or resale; (4) cargo and product-liability insurance policies; (5) external auditor attestation of internal-control design; (6) independent reconciliation of every EMI and PSP batch against invoice and dispatch records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant equity-injection protocol for a Spanish SL: (1) execute the corporate act before a Spanish notary (incorporation or capital increase), deposit the contribution, and register with the Registro Mercantil; (2) instruct the remitting bank to send SWIFT MT103 (cover MT202) with foreign-direct-investment equity purpose code, beneficiary stated as the SL with its Spanish NIF, and the deed number plus shareholder NIE in the narrative; (3) receive funds in the capital-deposit account at Banco Santander or CaixaBank, with the bank automatically filing the Banco de España statistical declaration for transactions at or above EUR 50,000; (4) submit Form DGI-01 to the Foreign Investment Registry within 30 days if cumulative foreign investment exceeds EUR 250,000, or if any tranche from a tax-haven jurisdiction exceeds EUR 50,000; (5) preserve the funds-received certificate and MT950 statement as proof of effective payment (desembolso). Equity must never be coded as a loan or trade payment to avoid recharacterisation and withholding-tax litigation. EMI-sourced inbound capital should be accompanied by a source-of-funds letter and routed through the primary Spanish bank account before deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Two-tier clearing design: (A) Eurozone and domestic disbursements use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT, T+1) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst, seconds, up to EUR 100,000) over Iberpay/local ACH rails with IBAN-only data, UETR references and structured remittance information, ideal for EU merchant refunds; (B) intercontinental trade settlements execute SWIFT MT103/MT101 customer credit transfers through the correspondent networks of BBVA or Santander, and for large or first-trade consignments use MT700 commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 supported by quality-grading certificates, cargo insurance and transport documents; (C) Airwallex virtual IBANs serve the high-frequency, low-value payout corridor to Latin-American warehouse agents using SPEI, PIX and local ACH, with automatic conversion of MXN and BRL proceeds into EUR, subject to full RMA/PO traceability and daily reconciliation to the primary Spanish account; (D) treasury policy prohibits an open FX position beyond five days, hedges all USD disbursements with forward cover, and requires an invoice, contract or returns-authorisation record for every outbound transfer above EUR 15,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright forwards with tenors up to 24 months under ISDA 2002 or Spanish AFB master agreements
Cash-settled EUR/GBP forwards and currency swaps
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted Latin-American currencies (MXN, BRL, ARS, COP) settled in USD
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) on EUR/USD and EUR/GBP for working-capital rebalancing
Plain-vanilla FX options (EUR call/USD put and USD call/EUR put) matching invoice cycles
Rolling NDF ladders for MXN and BRL to hedge reverse-logistics payout streams

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) and independent auditor's report if audited
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) in whose district the SL's registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting to approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year end; accounts deposited within 1 month of approval. For a calendar-year company: approval by 30 June; deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deposit: fine EUR 1,200 to EUR 6,000 (reduced to EUR 60 to EUR 600 if deposited before penalty order); registry folio is closed and other corporate inscriptions blocked; accounts cannot be relied on against third parties until deposited. Persistent failure for two consecutive years may reinforce the closure of the company's registry file and eventually lead to dissolution/inactivity proceedings under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalisation of statutory accounting books (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales and Libro Diario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year SL, by 30 April each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Books not legalised are defective evidence in commercial proceedings; the annual accounts deposit can be challenged; late legalisation requires a formalisation before the Mercantile Registry and may carry an additional registry tariff and negative note in the company's file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) - Form 200, including filing and payment of any corporate tax liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the close of the corporation tax period; if the fiscal year ends on 31 December, filing/payment deadline is 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing recargo: 5% to 20% of the payable tax depending on the delay; late-payment interest; infringement penalty of EUR 300 minimum or 15% of the assessed amount where no timely return was filed; persistent delinquency triggers enforcement action and inclusion in official tax debtor lists; not a direct strike-off event, but the registry file may be closed for failure to deposit annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return (Form 390) for SLs under the general VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 January to 30 January of the following calendar year (if the SL is subject to the general regime and files periodic VAT returns).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the VAT due plus late-payment interest; fixed penalty of EUR 200 to EUR 10,000 for non-filing or untimely filing after formal notice; loss of VAT deduction rights may be challenged by AEAT.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual information return on transactions with third parties (Form 347) - report of recipients/suppliers with annual transactions exceeding EUR 3,005.06
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last calendar day of February in the year following the reporting calendar year (28 or 29 February).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 150 per data item omitted or inaccurate, with a minimum fine of EUR 300; serious infringement if the omitted amount is material; false data may be re-assessed with surcharges of up to 20% of the net tax liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración de Titular Real, DTR) in the Registro de Titulares Reales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titulares Reales), managed through the Registro Mercantil and Colegio de Registradores
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year SL, by 31 March. Updated within 30 days after any relevant change in beneficial ownership or shareholding transfers of 5% or more.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law 10/2010 infringement penalties: up to EUR 60,000 for false, incomplete or omitted UBO information; the registry file may be blocked for other corporate filings until the DTR is updated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit of annual accounts is compulsory when the SL exceeds at least two of the following limits for two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees above 50. Audit is also triggered if shareholders representing at least 5% of the share capital so request through the Mercantile Registry, or when the SL belongs to a group that must produce consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Local GAAP: Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC) approved by RD 1514/2007. Individual annual accounts of an SL must be prepared under PGC; IFRS-EU applies only to consolidated financial statements of groups or in the voluntary cases permitted by the Ley de Auditoría de Cuentas.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must file an annual DTR declaration with the Registro de Titulares Reales even where no shareholding change has occurred. For SL quota transfers, transfer deeds must be recorded in the Libro Registro de Socios before the new quota holder is recognized; any change in direct or indirect ownership entailing a new or altered ultimate beneficial owner requires an updated DTR within 30 days of the transfer. The annual protocol must reconcile the list of UBOs (25%-or-more direct/indirect ownership or control) against the Register of Members, minutes of shareholder meetings, and the share transfer log, and must be submitted electronically through the Colegio de Registradores' portal.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and Officers (Libro Registro de Administradores)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 9,000 for a statutory audit if thresholds are met; no audit fee is budgeted if the SL qualifies for audit exemption
